- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots — apply a downward bias of 1–2% to subsequent forecasts.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment ambiguity.  
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising sharply, model is lagging — accelerate forecast slope to match sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage mean reversion — reduce forecast at end of horizon if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
